body:
## Change and rationale

This change completes the owner-selected retirement of legacy runtime support. `rigorloop-records-v2` is the only supported stored-record contract. `explicit-recording-v1`, `compact-current-state-v1`, `stage-owned-change-local-v1/v2/v3`, and `legacy-unversioned` no longer have runtime readers, creators, validators, mutation/progression handlers or recovery fallback. Their exclusive schemas, fixtures, positive acceptance tests, activation entries and directly affected consumers leave with the capability.

The owner confirmed legacy work is complete and v2 operates. That attributed operating baseline does not rewrite the earlier failed inventory/rollout observations as successful executions. No migration, temporary continuation or permanent archival reader was required. Historical change records, identities, judgments and published release evidence remain unchanged archives.

The approved Proposal, Record Format/CLI/Workflow Design package, and Delivery plan own direction and scope. M1 extracted neutral recording transport and project configuration helpers. M2 retained v2 storage and replaced discovery with bounded factual selection. M3 removed legacy engines and reconciled directly affected callers. M4 aligned governance, public guidance, document validators and generated candidate packages. The CLI retains mechanical storage authority; reviews and Verify retain independent substantive responsibilities.

## Exact basis and evidence

The registered subjects and final whole-change Code Review identify the complete engineering change, including the base identities of removed paths in their narrative inventory. The final assessment uses current approved Proposal/Design/Delivery evidence and the fresh independent complete-diff judgment. Earlier milestone judgments retain their original exact scope; stale historical applicability is not silently renewed or substituted for final review. All four implementation milestones and required corrections are complete. The original Design, discovery-diagnostic and manual-proof finding origins and their responsible reviewers' resolutions remain intact.

| Planned obligation | Realized protection and observed proof |
| --- | --- |
| TG-01: retained interfaces and independent versions | Neutral advanced/targeted transport and project configuration preserve the independent schema-1 document/request/result versions; schema generation and current Node/configuration tests pass. No name-based v1 purge of independent version domains. |
| TG-02: v2 storage/recovery and retired-input rejection | Full recording proof retains origin/reference namespaces, unknown-value rejection, identity/path safety, atomic publication, retry and recovery, correction recording and negative outcomes without semantic readiness gates. Recovery validates saved request/format basis, including absent-manifest initial creation; retired/unknown/inconsistent bases stop without guessed writes. |
| TG-03: factual current discovery | Complete discovery tests cover v2 candidates, malformed/ambiguous current roots, archives, safe paths/redaction and inclusive 1,024-directory/64-candidate/8-MiB bounds. No implicit selection or workflow judgment is added. |
| TG-04: legacy engine retirement | Public dispatch/help, exclusive modules/schemas/activation and positive acceptance proof are removed together. Surviving CLI tests exercise unsupported commands before logging, stdin reads or mutation and preserve current storage safety. |
| TG-05: callers and archival separation | Python metadata/query/lifecycle/automation/selector callers have explicit v2, removal or unsupported-before-effects dispositions. Full affected modules pass. New unreadable-archive regression failed before and passes after in both local and Git-snapshot validation; malformed selected v2 roots remain validated. |
| TG-06: current consumers and packages | Current canonical skills and selectively loaded resources describe v2; manual proof is registered evidence before successful Verify. Generated archives and candidate metadata match exact source. Full skill356, builder7 and installed npm7 pass, with fresh adapter validation and resource/source/candidate parity3 after final heading cleanup. |
| TG-FINAL-01: integrated result | All33 actual PR-range CI checks pass at the recorded immutable base/head. Fresh Node400 (zero skipped), full lifecycle110/review109/selector155, current package proof and full-branch whitespace checks support the delivered result. Independent whole-change review is separate from this evidence/coherence assessment. |

Actual integrated command: `bash scripts/ci.sh --mode pr --base e78bc3943d37092bd92997a2c9f06ea9d126e223 --head 879e2681b41fc35071f5514d3344d249aa27ecd9 --jobs 4`; 33 selected checks passed, including exact Git-snapshot lifecycle validation. `bash scripts/ci.sh --mode local --jobs 4` also passed after the archival-consumer correction. Exact commands, subject identities, environment, counts and removal inventory are stored in `final-helper-integrated-proof` and its referenced scoped evidence.

The fresh integrated run includes all final engineering corrections, including the helper bypass found during whole-change review. Every actual review Markdown reader now checks stored-input boundaries before content reads; direct automation helper callers cannot bypass them. Root validation and summarization preserve failure instead of constructing clean-looking empty evidence. Regression proof retains standalone review/log success, rejects stored v1/v2 bases and covers enclosing roots, symlink paths and unreadable markers. The reported real archived review now rejects with its three basis files unchanged. The full affected modules pass: review109, automation state13, automation31, automation validation68, code-state12, lifecycle110 and wrapper3.

Earlier EOF normalization was proved to remove only trailing newline bytes, preserving the Python AST and JS syntax. The heading-only cleanup has regenerated archives, full skill/builder tests and exact resource/source/candidate parity proof. Those changes are included in the latest full CI; no later engineering change is being inferred current from an old pass. Full adapter158 earlier passed; its unchanged builder/helper/release-profile protection is reused alongside fresh current resource/candidate and installation proof. No validation requirement is waived and no failed/interrupted run is counted as a pass.

Test removal follows the selected support contract and the approved Test model. Retired positive behavior needs no replacement demonstration that it still works. Required current safety and unsupported-input/no-mutation proof remain. Two obsolete source-string bundles mixed retired protocol placement with enduring review concerns; current v2 schema and specialist policy retain the latter protection. No general redundancy, runtime improvement, token reduction or coverage percentage is claimed.

Fresh final checks also run `node scripts/build-record-store-schema.mjs --check`, the approved three-model boundary validator, plan readability and full-branch `git diff --check`. Current record validation is structural proof only; it neither approves this assessment nor confers external authority.

## Limitations and residual risks

This is a deliberate compatibility break for the named retired stored formats and directly affected legacy execution callers. Broader automation/calibration and old release procedures remain outside scope except for their affected edges. Shared v2 dependencies remain supported. No historical approval becomes a current approval, and unrelated archives cannot block valid v2 work merely by being present. Malformed current v2 data is not dismissed as archival evidence.

All earlier change roots and published release evidence are unchanged in the final diff. Only current unpublished v0.5.1 candidate metadata and its index digest are regenerated; this does not publish a release. No migration service, new journal version, review stage, automatic policy engine or record type was introduced. Rollback is the coordinated source/consumer/package revert, preserving current v2 data and archival bytes.

Validation was observed locally on the environment recorded in evidence. Hosted CI is unobserved before initial PR creation and is not represented as passed; current PR policy permits submission with the required local readiness proof. Release publication, merge and destructive operations remain separately owned and are not performed. Existing unrelated lifecycle/readability warnings remain attributed baseline debt; touched governing package authority and required proof have been assessed separately. Successful closeout must not rely on older failed rollout or PR-check entries merely because they share a registered evidence file.


No separate Learn session is selected for this closeout: the concrete review misses, responsible dispositions and regression evidence remain in the owned findings and this explanation. Broader automation/calibration or release-procedure retirement remains a separately selected initiative.

## Observation disposition

Retained failed entries are rollout-audit (earlier operating-inventory attempt, superseded as decision basis by explicit owner confirmation, not rewritten as an executed pass) and m4-pr-range-failure (obsolete expectation/archive traversal failures corrected and freshly passed by full latest CI). Old subject drift belongs to historical evidence/reviews and immutable finding origins; exact required current review subjects and final engineering identities were reread and agree. No required current failure, open finding/blocker or unexplained current-subject drift supports this success. Completion can retain aggregate mechanical observations because earlier failed checks remain in the evidence file; their actual identities, causes and corrective proof were assessed rather than suppressed. Such an observation is not a CLI readiness decision. New contradictory evidence would require reassessment.
